title: Cubic Earth-velocity terms leave 10 to 59 percent of 377-day orbital information in 245 HD 1461 HARPS nights
abstract: We test Earth-velocity terms in 245 selected HD 1461 HARPS nights from RVBank version 02. A linear term reduces held-season error in DRS minus SERVAL velocities by 6.71 percent after nightly corrections and 22.26 percent before them. Cubic terms give smaller gains. A separate design calculation shows that fitting cubic Earth-velocity terms to stellar velocities leaves only 10.19 to 58.53 percent of the information about a circular 377-day signal, depending on phase. Explicit injected signals check the bounds. The known short-period signals retain at least 95.59 percent. This is a version-specific data audit and method test, not a new planet or a new cause for the known annual HARPS error. The reductions share spectra. A common instrument error can remain in both. The calculation assumes stated weights and season offsets, and is not a detection probability. We include code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps. Source rows are excluded. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-b398203a0f6c; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Held-season prediction of corrected DRS minus SERVAL differences, and orbital information left after cubic Earth-velocity terms. The bounds vary with orbital phase and use the selected 245-night sampling.
